question.worked_solution:
First, remember that a fraction represents a division:

$$
\frac{\,\,(-4)\,\,}{(\frac{1}{5})}=(-4)÷\frac{1}{5}
$$

Now, recall that $-4=-\frac{4}{1}$ and dividing by $\frac{1}{5}$ is the same as multiplying by its reciprocal $\frac{5}{1}.$ We can use these facts to simplify the fraction above:  

$$
\begin{aligned}(-4)÷\frac{1}{5} & = \\ (-\frac{4}{1})\times \frac{5}{1} & = \\ -\frac{4\times 5}{1\times 1} & = \\ -\frac{20}{1} & = \\ -20 & \end{aligned}
$$

 

Therefore,

$$
\frac{\,\,(-4)\,\,}{(\frac{1}{5})}=-20.
$$
